title: v0.33.0
summary:
v0.33.0

Highlights

This release features 927 commits from 389 contributors (122 new)!

  • New models: Reflection Beam-1.0 (501B MoE, 23B active) with its DFlash2 drafter (#62074), Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (#57963), Recursive Flint (40B MoE, 2.5B active) (#62938), Muse Spark Open (#61879), Step-5 Preview (#61727, #63147), NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957), Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149), Nemotron Parse 3.5 (#61651), MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095), Domyn Edge (#62544) and the ColUltraVBERT visual document retriever (#62237).
  • PyTorch 2.14: vLLM is upgraded to PyTorch 2.14.0, with torchvision 0.29.0 and Triton 3.8.0 (#52183).
  • CUDA 12.9 dropped: release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only. The CUDA 12.9 wheels and the -cu129 / -cu129-ubuntu2404 images are no longer published (#62575); use the default CUDA 13.0 artifacts instead.
  • libtorch ABI stable CUDA wheel: the CUDA wheel is now ABI stable with libtorch.
  • AWS EFA image: a new vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa image (x86_64 and aarch64) bundles the AWS EFA libraries and the EFA build of the Mooncake transfer engine, for KV transfer and multi-node serving on EFA-enabled EC2 instances (#58768).
  • vllm/vllm image alias: every release image is now also published under the shorter vllm/vllm name, e.g. vllm/vllm:v0.33.0, vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa and vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm.
  • Speculative decoding: the new XPress refiner for block-diffusion drafters such as DFlash and DSpark (#54448); FLy, an opt-in lossy verification policy with 1.04-1.31x decode throughput on MI355X and B300 (#53987); DFlash/DSpark no longer reserve draft slots in the token budget, taking DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on GB300 from 1373 to 3390 output tok/s in the PR's benchmark (#59468); quantized draft lm_head (draft_lm_head_quantization, +18% decode at concurrency 1) (#59973); lookahead block hashes so EAGLE/MTP prefix-cache hits keep their last block, on by default (#61589); and MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend (#61270).
  • Faster decode on NVIDIA: opt-in latency-specialized decode on GB300 for Kimi-K3 (1.5-2x at TP8/TP16, #61867) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (18.3% faster decode step at batch 1, #61868); DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 experts run as block FP8 through Humming on Hopper (+9-21% decode on 4x H200, #61875); FA4 sparse MLA decode on Blackwell (#55866); FlashInfer DCP prefill on trtllm-gen with 39-48% lower mean TTFT at 100k input on 8xB200 (#62029); and decode-only full CUDA graphs under MRV2 prefill context parallelism (2.6x over eager, #62377).
  • AMD ROCm: the default ROCm image and wheels move to ROCm 10.0, with ROCm 7.2 still published as -rocm72 (#58761); MonoKernel decode via --monokernel for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI300X/MI325X (2.32x P50 interactivity at concurrency 1, #60731) and on every MI355X layer (#61082), and for MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on MI355X (16.6% lower TPOT, #62712, #62994); the ROCM_OCTAVE 3-4 bit KV cache (4.6x the KV tokens of fp16 on RX 7900 XTX, #59774); and gfx1250 enablement for gpt-oss-120b, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 (#58800).
  • API and serving: the OpenAI-compatible /v1/decisions endpoint, on by default for supported generation models (#60465, #61550); token embeddings with optional late chunking on /v1/embeddings (#61772, #63051, #60164); output_mode="derender" on /inference/v1/generate (#60082); a large Rust frontend parity push, including no more HTTP 500 on long conversations (#62374) and unsupported flags failing at startup (#62431); concurrent worker startup with TP > 1 (#60028); and a watchdog that dumps stack traces from stuck engine and worker processes (#55700).
  • Breaking changes: Medusa and the MLP speculator removed (#61701); the legacy Ray compiled-graph executor removed (#61712, #62228); --mamba-cache-mode deprecated (#60043); requests sent while generation is paused now get HTTP 503 (#51488); the NIXL connector needs NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032); LM Format Enforcer and --ir-op-priority deprecated (#63423, #63371).

Other Artifacts

Pre-built release artifacts are available in the Assets section at the bottom of this page, including:

  • Source distribution tarball
  • CUDA 13.0 Python wheels for x86_64 and arm64
  • CPU Python wheels for x86_64, arm64, and macOS
  • XPU Python wheel for x86_64

Model Support

  • New models: Reflection Beam-1.0 (BeamForCausalLM) day-0 support with its DFlash2 drafter and fused Blackwell kernels (#62074, #62042), plus beam reasoning and tool parsers (#62052); Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (Kimi Delta Attention hybrid, 512-expert MoE, 262K context) (#57963); Recursive Flint BF16 and NVFP4 GGUF checkpoints with small-batch Blackwell decode kernels (#62938); Muse Spark Open (#61879) with reasoning and tool parsers (#62207); Step-5 Preview (#61727, #62126, #62132), running on SM100 (#63147) with LoRA (#62498); NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957); Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149); Nemotron Parse 3.5 with an MTP proposer on MRV2 (#61651); MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095); Domyn Edge (#62544); ColUltraVBERT (#62237); LFM2.5-Embedding-350M (Lfm2BidirectionalModel, #62201); Kolibri 1 through the Transformers backend (#60827); and Decision 3.0 models (#61565, #61778) and Cloudflare Clef-Flash (#61308) on /v1/systemone.
  • DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1: length-aware decode indexer block selection (about 850 us saved per step at 1M context, #61039); MegaMoE experts loaded directly in the DeepGEMM layout so reload_weights works (#60096); fused_wqa_wkv split by token across TP on SM90 (#58872); MegaAttn wo_a writes MXFP8 input for wo_b (#60118); native small-head FlashMLA sparse prefill on SM90 (#61615); FlashMLA interleaved KV layout (#61371); redundant EPLB expert slots loaded (#59611); GPU Engram tables read from peer HBM, fixing DEP decode hangs on GB200 (#62091); and fixes for Engram under PP (#62208), Engram all-to-all hangs (#62269), prefill index-workspace NaNs (#60613), C128 compressed-KV writes under PIECEWISE graphs (#59709), routed-expert rows under replay (#61643, #62652) and the updated 1017 reference encoding (#62199, #62200).
  • GLM: GLM-5.3-Flash defaults to an FP8 KV cache (9.8% higher end-to-end throughput in the PR's benchmark, #61228) and gets mHC TileLang decode kernels on Blackwell (#62745); GLM-5.3 per-token-group quant (2.8% ITL, #60927), in-place draft decode metadata (#61873) and skipped concat_and_cache_mla scales (1.2-3.0% TPOT on B300, #62102); FP8 indexer WK pairs kept across load_weights calls, fixing thinking loops with runai_streamer (#59223).
  • Kimi-K3: KDA RecoverSSM CuTe DSL verify/commit kernels on SM10x, with verify records moved out of the KV cache so KV connectors work (#63045); online quantization of NVIDIA projections (#62980).
  • Qwen: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 QSA KV cache on Ampere (#60602, #60992), packed NVFP4 PLE embeddings that fit Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on one DGX Spark (#56273) and PLE short-conv prefill checkpoints (#61601); FlashInfer GDN prefill checkpoints for Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 (#60050).
  • Other models: Cohere2MoE attention/MoE dual stream, single TP all-reduce and fused add + RMSNorm (1.14-1.36x TPOT, on by default, #62101); Beam TP all-reduce fused with norms and MoE finalize (#62366); MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS MSA decode crossover (#55838); Granite MoE as an EAGLE3/DFlash/DSpark target (#61110); NemotronHMTP sharing target embeddings (#62194); LoRA for BERT cross-encoders and token classification (#61279, #61391).
  • Multimodal: PaddleOCR-VL batched vision encoder (34-85% more throughput, #61458) and compile_mm_encoder (#61838); DeepSeek-VL2 ViT full CUDA graphs (#46005); Gemma4Unified batched embedding (#60643); Pixtral real-valued RoPE under compile (#63145); and fixes for EXAONE-4.5 images (broken since v0.29.0, #61104), Gemma 4 encoder graphs (#61365, #60687, #63538), DeepSeek-VL2 encoder cache and PP (#63120, #63192) and Gemma 4 placeholders (#61196).
  • Transformers modeling backend: MTP speculative drafts (#61270), fused post-top-k MoE routers (#57410), graph caching instead of AOT caching (#58918) and dynamic-RoPE CUDA graphs (#58064).

Engine Core

  • Speculative decoding: XPress (#54448), FLy (#53987), no draft-slot budget reservation for DFlash/DSpark (#59468), quantized draft lm_head (#59973), lookahead block hashes (#61589), MRV2 skipping drafts no request can use (up to 7.3% prefill throughput with DFlash, #62784), Triton split-K verify (#56148), varlen Mamba2 decode for adaptive verification (#53036), and fixes for stop-trimmed token counts (#58668), block verification randomness (#61161), MTP block tables (#61174), grammar masks (#52477), EAGLE SWA prefix hits (#62206), DFlash/DSpark Mamba checkpoint reuse (#54163) and PP warmup (#62129).
  • Model Runner V2: batch-sharded sampling for GPT-OSS (#61257) with adaptive verification (#58466), 31-120x faster long-prompt staged writes on GB200 (#62698), encoder towers skipped on later PP stages (0.58-1.27 GiB per stage, #60238), async scheduling kept for ngram (#62521), input_ids on later PP stages (#61016), and memory-profiling fixes (#57926, #58243, #61509, #63431).
  • Sampling: Triton top-k/top-p skips the cutoff search for masked logits (up to about 8x, #61213); small-batch split top-p (1.22-2.70x on B300, #61996); and fixes for huge logits and boundary ties (#58231, #62046).
  • Startup and reliability: concurrent local worker startup with TP > 1 (about 50s saved at TP8, #60028); shared Triton JIT compile pool (9-28% faster cold warmup, #61422); engine and worker watchdog (#55700); libgomp fork deadlock fixed (#62884); Fast Start with expert parallelism (#55490) and daemon fixes (#62583, #63451, #63088, #62734, #63506); and SHM broadcast reader memory growth fixed (#63165).
  • Memory and performance: UVA-offloaded MoE experts on the sorted fused-MoE path (+7-19%, #62054); DispatchPooler bypass for homogeneous pooling (up to 10.3%, #62940); linear-time encoder cache free (#62850); sliding-window block tables null freed entries (#60767).
  • LoRA: expert LoRA for MXFP4 MoE on flashinfer_trtllm (#61979), text-only LoRAs on multimodal wrappers (#62224), unsupported models rejected at validation (#61884), and fixes for load_inplace reloads (#41482), max_loras accounting (#60306), SM90 lora_expand NaNs (#61906) and wake-up from level-2 sleep (#62358).
  • RL: per-choice return_weight_versions (#61347), NCCL M2N transfer with per-parameter meshes (#60934), parameter metadata sent once (#35911), the ParamMeta / iter_full() / iter_local() weight-transfer API (#63256), and a silent MoE weight corruption fix with packed NCCL transfer plus layerwise reload (#62555).
  • Batch invariance: compressed-tensors W4A16/W8A16 (#60524), GateLinear routers (#59985), online FP8 MoE (#57092), and inductor batch-invariant mode under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT (#61118).

Large Scale Serving

  • Context parallelism: MRV2 PCP decode full CUDA graphs (#62377); PCP for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with prefix caching and SWA bounded replay (#59857, #62183, #62384); FlashInfer DCP prefill on trtllm-gen (#62029); direct DCP all-to-all with strided LSE (#60373); FlashMLA sparse on the a2a DCP backend (#61285).
  • HiSparse: direct reads of GPU-resident KV, fixing OOM with long prompts and a 3.3x slowdown on 1M-token prefill (#60417); faster host pool prefault (#60869); and P/D correctness fixes (#61659, #62739, #63827).
  • KV connectors: NIXL 1.5 strided descriptors (#61032), sleep mode with the pull connector (#59635), mixed hybrid MLA block sizes (#61002) and GQA draft head sharding (#58471); Mooncake sleep mode over RDMA (#59625) and Prometheus metrics (#56939); MoRIIO hybrid and heterogeneous-TP WRITE transfers (#60544, #61726); streaming responses carry kv_transfer_params (#40186); fault tolerance extended to P/D, fixing KV block leaks (#56430).
  • KV offload: CPU offload over up to 32 shm files (GLM-5.3 offload startup 63.6 s to 38.3 s, #59546), opt-in same-step small loads (#61961), EAGLE/MTP partial tails in align mode (#61019), lock/unlock and off-thread tiering (#58168), and many correctness fixes (#63266, #60810, #63652, #62929, #63010, #60574, #63655).
  • MoE and DP: DeepEP-v2 fused decode globalize+align (up to 2.01x on H200 EP32, #53911); Elastic EP with an external load balancer (#43202); low-latency CPU all-reduce for DP syncs (#61767) and a DP wave hang fix (#59559); EPLB fixes for MXFP4/MXFP8 scales (#61786) and NIXL reads (#62081).

Hardware & Performance

  • NVIDIA: Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash latency-specialized decode on GB300 (#61867, #61868); FA4 sparse MLA decode (#55866); opt-in CuTe DSL MLA context prefill (#62069); DeepGEMM MegaMoE with NVFP4 routed experts (#61538) and warmed-up kernels (#60468, #61657); Triton GDN decode tuned on SM100 (#61355); GLM-5.2/5.3 low-latency BF16 GEMM on SM107 (#62843); pre-SM90 FlashInfer spec decode in full CUDA graphs (73.6 to 108.1 tok/s on SM80, #60532); cooperative_topk sized by row length (#62171); fused GDN MTP decode for SM80-SM90 in CUDA 12.x builds (#60896); and DGX Spark Qwen4Exp TP2 plans (#61437).
  • AMD ROCm: ROCm 10.0 default image (#58761); MonoKernel decode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and V4-Pro and MiniMax-M3 (#60731, #61082, #61482, #62712, #62994); ROCM_OCTAVE KV cache (#59774); gfx1250 enablement (#58800); DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 indexer K cache by default on CDNA4 (up to 30.7% lower TTFT, #60834, #63669); AITER MegaMoE fixed-slot dispatch (14-15%, #61262) and shared-expert overlap (#61819); Kimi-K3 Gluon KDA kernels (#57392, #59552) and specialized decode (#60683); Qwen3.5 fused GDN MTP decode (+10-16% on MI350X, #61855); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next native W4A4 (1.9-2.3x, #60816); AITER top-k for sparse indexers on gfx950 (#61943); FlyDSL GDN prefill default on gfx942/gfx950 (#60645); RDNA3 TRITON_ATTN addressing restored (about 18%, #60084); and a MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 startup fix for very large GEMMs (#64567).
  • Intel XPU: SYCL GDN prefill backend selection (#56835), torch MXFP4 linear backend (#51965), SYCL FlashAttention for prefix-LM text batches (#62014) and NIXL 1.5.0 in the image (#60356).
  • CPU: zentorch 2.14.0.1 with float16 on Zen CPUs with AVX512-FP16 (#61411); MRV2 Triton warmup at startup removing an 11-20 s first-request compile (#62888); INT8 W8A8 MoE brgemm (#60740); hybrid-model prefix caching (#61805); and Run:ai Model Streamer in the CPU image (#61382).
  • Other: tpu-inference v0.32.0 with torch 2.14.0 (#63080) and more out-of-tree platform hooks (#62026, #63017, #63601, #63457).

Quantization

  • Humming runs DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 experts as block FP8 on Hopper (#61875) and honors --quantization-config.moe.activation (#62751); pluggable KV cache data types (#52670); online re-quantization extended to NVFP4 MoE (#60276); Quark MXFP8 routed experts (#63125); MoNe expert-pruning checkpoints (#50415); torch MXFP8 linear backend (#51933); FP8 per-token-group quant 1.15-1.29x faster (#61343); Cosmos3-Edge ModelOpt FP8 (#57393); and a Nemotron-3-Nano NVFP4 garbage-output fix under torch.compile (#61749).

API & Frontend

  • New endpoints and options: /v1/decisions (#60465, #61550); token embeddings and late chunking (#61772, #63051, #60164); output_mode="derender" (#60082); --reasoning-effort-map (#61094); --sleep-mode-backend (#63138); dynamic profiler options on /start_profile (#51974); images on /v1/systemone (#62181, #62437); Responses max_tool_calls (#47112) and prompt-cache fields (#62856); and /openapi.json response schemas (#60926).
  • Tool calling and reasoning: linear-time streaming tool arguments for GLM, Gemma 4, Qwen3 XML (2.1 s to 11 ms for a 12 KB call) and MiniMax M2 (#61253, #61494, #62027, #62035); DeepSeek V3 multi-line arguments (#60362); structured output masks grammar-invalid reasoning ends instead of returning 500 (#61574).
  • Behavior: chat finish_reason and Responses status reflect what happened (#59324); beam search normalizes by generated length so length_penalty applies (#62928); automatic truncation reserves one generation token (#62010).
  • Rust frontend: --trust-request-chat-template (#62673), --return-tokens-as-token-ids (#63318), --tokenizer options (#62416), --custom-histogram-buckets (#62826) and per-request metrics (#59314); request and response parity with the Python frontend (#62434, #62425, #62426, #62427, #62428, #61949, #62429, #62822, #62663); and the MiniJinja fuel limit only on request-supplied templates (#62374).

Security

  • Per-request budgets for downloaded and decoded media bytes (#61226); speculators checkpoint metadata can no longer reference local verifier paths (#61587); certifi>=2026.10.19 and refreshed CA certificates (#62868); raised floors for aiohttp, Pillow, MCP and multidict (#62835).

Dependencies

  • PyTorch 2.14.0, torchvision 0.29.0, Triton 3.8.0 (#52183).
  • FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (#60948, #61913, #63466), humming-kernels 0.1.19 (#62816, #64802), DeepGEMM 2.8.1 and later pins (#61149, #61744, #63253), FlashMLA 2026.09.30 (#61371), TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3 (#61125, #61689), nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.31.0 (#61465), NIXL 1.5.0 (#60428, #60356) and LMCache 0.5.6 (#62835).
  • ROCm: AITER v0.1.26 (#61697, #62486) and UCX v1.23.0-rc1 (#62827). CPU: zentorch 2.14.0.1 (#61411). TPU: tpu-inference v0.32.0 (#63080).

Build

  • Release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only (#62575); new vllm-openai-efa Docker target (#58768); ROCm 10.0 is the default ROCm image with ROCm 7.2 as -rocm72 (#58761); ROCm wheel builds about 4-7x faster (#63105).

Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • CUDA 12.9 wheels and images are no longer published (#62575).
  • Medusa and the MLP speculator were removed (#61701). The legacy Ray compiled-graph executor was removed and VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND is gone; RayExecutorV2 is the only Ray executor (#61712, #62228).
  • Deprecated: --mamba-cache-mode (no effect, #60043), --ir-op-priority (removal in v0.34.0, #63371), and the LM Format Enforcer structured-output backend (opt-in in v0.34.0, removal in v0.35.0, #63423).
  • API changes: requests sent while generation is paused return HTTP 503 (#51488); kv_transfer_params / ec_transfer_params moved to the top level of render output (#61241); LoRA on a model without LoRA support fails at validation (#61884); the RL weight-transfer API now uses ParamMeta, iter_full() and iter_local() (#63256); beam search scores are normalized by generated length (#62928).
  • Rust frontend: unsupported vllm serve flags and request fields fail instead of being ignored (#62431, #62434); request-supplied chat templates need --trust-request-chat-template (#62673); an empty tools array returns 400 (#63060).
  • The NIXL connector requires NIXL 1.5 or newer (#61032).
  • Removed env vars: VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY (#61628), VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM (#61278) and VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS (#61345); VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE is replaced by --monokernel (#61082).
  • New defaults: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 KV cache (#61228); lookahead block hashes for EAGLE/MTP prefix caching (#61589); Cohere2MoE dual stream (#62101); FA4 sparse MLA decode at 16 or fewer query heads per rank on Blackwell (#55866); ROCm: AITER FP8/FP4 BMM for MLA off (#53123), FlyDSL GDN prefill (#60645), AITER topk_gating (#56226), rms_norm_gated (#60250) and MXFP4 indexer K cache on CDNA4 for DeepSeek-V4 (#63669).

title: Release 2.75.0 corresponding to NGC container 26.11
summary:
Triton Inference Server

The Triton Inference Server provides a cloud inferencing solution optimized for both CPUs and GPUs. The server provides an inference service via an HTTP or GRPC endpoint, allowing remote clients to request inferencing for any model being managed by the server. For edge deployments, Triton Server is also available as a shared library with an API that allows the full functionality of the server to be included directly in an application.

New Features and Improvements

  • PyTorch backend: Added AOTI BF16 input/output support.
  • THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt is now included in the containers.
  • Fixed a use-after-free in the dynamic batcher and a preserve_ordering completion-slot issue on response-cache hits.
  • Prevented silent gRPC stream cancellations under backpressure.
  • Bounded the decompressed HTTP inference response size in the client library.
  • Perf Analyzer: Honored supplied output shapes, propagated the binary exit code, tagged the wheel as platform-specific, and limited profile-data export to the needed inputs and outputs.
  • Python backend: Now logs when the backend stub exits on a crash signal.

Known Issues

  • The Triton TensorRT-LLM Backend container image is not included in this release.
  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:
    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.
  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen.
  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry.
  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.
  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.
  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.
  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ....
  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.
  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.
  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. In attempt to load a vllm model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vllm related sub-processes are not killed. Related vllm issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766. Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vllm models with tensor parallelism > 1.
  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".
  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.
  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.
  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.
  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. Tcmalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.
  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.
  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names matches what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: pytorch/pytorch#38273
  • Triton Client PIP wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.
  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.
  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.
  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

Client Libraries and Examples

The client libraries and examples are available in this release exclusively via the Ubuntu 24.04–based NGC Container. The SDK container includes the client libraries and examples, Performance Analyzer, and Model Analyzer. See Getting the Client Libraries for more information.

ManyLinux Assets (early access)

This release was compiled with AlmaLinux 8.9 based out of manylinux_2_34 and can be used on RHEL 9 and later versions.
See the included README.md for complete details about installation, verification, and support.
This release supports ensembles. Confirm CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, PyTorch, and Python versions in the shipped README.md.
Some optional backend features such as the PyTorch backend's TorchTRT extension are not currently supported.

  • Core: Improved model-readiness reporting in TRITONSERVER_ServerModelIsReady — non-availability errors are now returned, unresolved models correctly report ready=false, and the readiness lookup is * resolved by ModelIdentifier.
  • Python backend: Fixed a deadlock in decoupled BLS and a use-after-free in the async_exec pybind callback.
  • Security: Restriction header values are now redacted from the OpenAI frontend startup log, and the inference restriction is enforced in the SageMaker MME invoke handler.

Known Issues

  • Avoid the specific APIs/flows (low-level OCB, BIO_f_linebuffer with short writes, CMS password-based decryption, low-level GF(2^m) with untrusted params) for many linux binaries, in order to avoid exposure to known issues in OpenSSL 1.1.1.
  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:
    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.
  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen.
  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry.
  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.
  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.
  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.
  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ....
  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.
  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.
  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. In attempt to load a vllm model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vllm related sub-processes are not killed. Related vllm issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766. Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vllm models with tensor parallelism > 1.
  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".
  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.
  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.
  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.
  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. Tcmalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.
  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.
  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names matches what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: pytorch/pytorch#38273
  • Triton Client PIP wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.
  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.
  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.
  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

  • Fixed a race condition in AddNextResponse for concurrent streaming responses when cancelling requests.

  • Fixed ensemble requests that could remain stuck indefinitely when a step's max_queue_size was exceeded.

  • Added model name validation for model management requests.

  • Introduced safe GetElementCount and GetByteSize APIs with proper validation and overflow protection (including fixes in the common library).

  • Restored a model-instance code path that had been accidentally removed in a recent commit.

  • PyTorch backend — AOT Inductor (PT2): Full support for PyTorch PT2 format model archives using AOT Inductor: new platform torch_aoti with default model file model.pt2; new provider classes InductorModel and InductorModelInstance; pytorch_libtorch and torch_aoti separated into distinct namespaces; helper utilities, macros, TritonException, and optional debug trace logging (ENABLE_DEBUG_TRACE_*); complements the existing pytorch_libtorch platform and model.pt workflow.

  • Python backend: Support for a user-defined is_ready() in readiness checks for custom health logic in Python models.

  • ONNX Runtime backend: Enabled bfloat16 I/O tensor dtype support; updated the ONNX Runtime generation script (removed obsolete Windows and iGPU references, sourced TensorRT version from the container image, updated OpenVINO and Python versions, installed ccache, improved RHEL image installation steps and build reliability).

  • Client: Relaxed the upper bound on the gRPC dependency for flexibility; added requirements bounds checks; updated jackson-databind for security.

  • Model Analyzer: Updated default branch tracking and packaging for 1.52.0 / 26.03.

  • TensorRT-LLM backend: Documentation for multi-instance configuration with llmapi; updated TensorRT-LLM build versions, dependencies, and submodule (e.g. release/1.2); updated base images; fixed broken package installations during build; added torchgen for torch package compatibility; adjusted PyTorch dependency wrapping, setuptools, and related submodule versions.

  • vLLM backend: Addressed an API compatibility issue.

  • Testing: Added L0_backend_onnxruntime coverage for bfloat16 dtype; warmed up the CUDA cache before tests in L0_batcher for GB300 runners; added tests for the safe GetElementCount and GetByteSize APIs; fixed misuse of a log file argument in tests; refreshed development versions and documentation.

Known Issues

  • Avoid the specific APIs/flows (low-level OCB, BIO_f_linebuffer with short writes, CMS password-based decryption, low-level GF(2^m) with untrusted params) for Manylinux binaries, in order to avoid exposure to known issues in OpenSSL 1.1.1.

  • Since 25.10, the vLLM backend uses the V1 engine by default. You might see invalid characters in logprobs output; the issue has been reported to the vLLM team.

  • The PyTorch backend supports PyTorch 2.0 with the limitation that models must be provided as a serialized model file (aka model.pt). AOT Inductor models use platform torch_aoti and model.pt2 as documented for this release. Please see the Triton PyTorch Backend documentation for details.

  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:

    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.

  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen. The root cause has been identified and fixed in CUDA.

  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry. The root cause is under investigation.

  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.

  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.

  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.

  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics: tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ...

  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.

  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.

  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. When loading a vLLM model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at the initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vLLM-related sub-processes are not killed. Related vLLM issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766. Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vLLM models with tensor parallelism > 1.

  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of a custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".

  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.

  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.

  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.

  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. TCMalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.

  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.

  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names match what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: pytorch/pytorch#38273

  • Triton Client pip wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of the Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.

  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.

  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.

  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

Client Libraries and Examples

The client libraries and examples are available in this release exclusively via the Ubuntu 24.04–based NGC Container. The SDK container includes the client libraries and examples, Performance Analyzer, and Model Analyzer. See Getting the Client Libraries for more information.

Triton TRT-LLM Container Support Matrix

The Triton TensorRT-LLM container image and base layers are updated for this release. Please refer to the support matrix and compatibility.md in the TensorRT-LLM backend repository for all dependency versions.

Dependency Version
TensorRT-LLM 1.2.0
TensorRT See compatibility.md for the TensorRT version pinned to the 26.03 TRT-LLM container

ManyLinux Assets (early access)

This release was compiled with AlmaLinux 8.9 based out of manylinux_2_28 and can be used on RHEL 8 and later versions.
See the included README.md for complete details about installation, verification, and support.
This release supports ensembles. Confirm CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, PyTorch, and Python versions in the shipped README.md.
Some optional backend features such as the PyTorch backend's TorchTRT extension are not currently supported.

title: Release 2.66.0 corresponding to NGC container 26.02
summary:
Triton Inference Server

The Triton Inference Server provides a cloud inferencing solution optimized for both CPUs and GPUs. The server provides an inference service via an HTTP or GRPC endpoint, allowing remote clients to request inferencing for any model being managed by the server. For edge deployments, Triton Server is also available as a shared library with an API that allows the full functionality of the server to be included directly in an application.

Important

Triton 26.02 is the last Triton release for Jetson platform devices on GitHub.

New Features and Improvements

  • Fixed and updated broken links and anchors in documents across repositories.

  • Fixed broken page links on Nvidia Triton Inference Server Documentation.

  • Fixed an issue where unbound output size from a model could lead to resource exhaustion and denial of service. (#8603)

  • Fixed an issue where malformed HTTP header could cause a server crash (#8637)

Known Issues

  • Avoid the specific APIs/flows (low-level OCB, BIO_f_linebuffer with short writes, CMS password-based decryption, low-level GF(2^m) with untrusted params) for Manylinux binaries, in order to avoid exposure to known issues in OpenSSL 1.1.1.

  • Since 25.10, vLLM backend uses V1 engine by default. You might see invalid characters in logprobs output and the bug has been reported to the vLLM team.

  • PyTorch backend supports PyTorch 2.0 with the limitation that models must be provided as a serialized model file (aka ‘model.pt’). Please see Triton PyTorch Backend documentation for details.

  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:

    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.

  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen. The root cause has been identified and fixed in CUDA.

  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry. The root cause is under investigation.

  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.

  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.

  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.

  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ...

  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.

  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.

  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. In attempt to load a vllm model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vllm related sub-processes are not killed. Related vllm issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766 . Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vllm models with tensor parallelism > 1.

  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".

  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.

  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.

  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.

  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. TCMalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.

  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.

  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names matches what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/38273

  • Triton Client PIP wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.

  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.

  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.

  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

Client Libraries and Examples

Ubuntu 24.04 builds of the client libraries and examples are included in this release in the attached v2.66.0_ubuntu2404.clients.tar.gz file. The SDK is also available for as an Ubuntu 24.04 based NGC Container. The SDK container includes the client libraries and examples, Performance Analyzer and Model Analyzer. Some components are also available in the tritonclient pip package. See Getting the Client Libraries for more information on each of these options.

Jetson iGPU Support

A release of Triton for IGX is provided in the attached tar file: tritonserver2.66.0-igpu.tar.

  • This release supports CUDA 12.9, TensorRT 10.11.0.33, Onnx Runtime 1.24.1, PyTorch [2.11.0a0+eb65b36](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/frameworks/install-pytorch-jetson-platform-release-notes/pytorch-jetson-rel.html), **Python** 3.12` and as well as ensembles.
  • ONNX Runtime backend does not support the OpenVINO and TensorRT execution providers. The CUDA execution provider is in Beta.
  • System shared memory is supported on Jetson. CUDA shared memory is not supported.
  • GPU metrics, GCS storage, S3 storage and Azure storage are not supported.

The tar file contains the Triton server executable and shared libraries and also the C++ and Python client libraries and examples. For more information on how to install and use Triton on JetPack refer to jetson.md.

The wheel for the Python client library is present in the tar file and can be installed by running the following command:

python3 -m pip install --upgrade clients/python/tritonclient-2.66.0-py3-none-manylinux2014_aarch64.whl[all]

Jetson AGX Systems Support

A release of Triton for AGX Systems is provided in the attached tar file: tritonserver2.66.0-agx.tar.

  • This release supports CUDA 13.1, TensorRT 10.15.1.29, Onnx Runtime 1.24.1, PyTorch 2.11.0a0+eb65b36, Python 3.12 and as well as ensembles.

  • This package is a subset of nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:26.02-py3 ARM container image assets it.

Triton TRT-LLM Container Support Matrix

The Triton TensorRT-LLM container is built from the 25.10 image nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:25.10-py3-min. Please refer to the support matrix and compatibility.md for all dependency versions related to 25.10. However, the packages listed below have different versions than those specified in the support matrix.

Dependency Version
TensorRT-LLM 1.1.0
TensorRT 10.13.3.9

ManyLinux Assets (early access)

This release was compiled with AlmaLinux 8.9 based out of manylinux_2_28 and can be used on RHEL8 and later versions.
See the included README.md for complete details about installation, verification, and support.
This release supports CUDA 13, TensorRT 10.15.1.29, Onnx Runtime 1.24.1, PyTorch 2.11.0a0+eb65b36, Python 3.12 and supports ensembles.
Some optional backend features such as the PyTorch backend's TorchTRT extension are not currently supported.

title: v2.1.332
summary:
What's changed

  • Added skills from MCP servers (beta). They show as server:skill in the / menu; other skills keep their names
  • Added a PreSkillShellCommand hook event that can refuse a skill or command's inline shell commands as it loads; on 2.1.331 and older, a settings file naming it opens a dialog at start
  • Added "Always deliver" to the prompt for held messages from other sessions
  • Added a footer line that stays while a flagged message has your session on a different model, until you pick one with /model
  • Added an OpenTelemetry assistant_response event for text Claude sends through SendUserMessage or Cowork's message tool, when response logging is on
  • Added a warning in VS Code and Desktop's Code tab when part of a session couldn't be saved, saying how to save it with /compact
  • Added a notice in VS Code and Desktop's Code tab when a resumed session's earlier messages weren't loaded, as the terminal already shows
  • Added your Cyber Verification Program access tier to the startup header, beside the model name when your tier applies to that model and you're signed in with a claude.ai account
  • Fixed claude auth login reporting Login successful. when a claude.ai login could not be saved: it now exits 1 and says what to check, such as a leftover lock file or a full disk
  • Fixed Read, @-mentions and compaction hanging on a named pipe that nothing writes to, such as a .env mounted by a locked secrets manager; the read now fails after 20 seconds
  • Fixed turns ending in "Prompt is too long" after repeated auto-compaction failures when one more compaction at the context limit could have kept them going
  • Fixed compaction failing when a summary kept running past the output limit: after three cut-off replies, the last try now asks for a shorter summary
  • Fixed a freeze when a permission rule or hook condition with several wildcards was checked against a long command
  • Fixed freezes and runaway memory use in most cases while a hook prints output without end
  • Fixed a freeze and context overflow when a hook blocks or fails during a turn, or after /compact, with a very large log; text over about 50,000 characters is now shortened
  • Fixed the terminal freezing, and ignoring Ctrl+C, while a local MCP server floods its standard output
  • Fixed a freeze when a prompt or piped input holds an @ followed by a very long unbroken string, such as minified CSS with an embedded font
  • Fixed a long freeze when opening a rewind point after a large tracked file was rewritten
  • Fixed SSE MCP servers hanging or refusing every tool call after their event stream was cut and came back on a new endpoint or not at all, until reconnected by hand
  • Fixed Remote Control showing a session in the desktop app, VS Code or the Agent SDK as running while it waited there on a dialog or an MCP server's question
  • Fixed a usage limit being reported as reached to Remote Control, IDE and SDK clients after it had already reset
  • Fixed CLAUDE.md and rules files being sent to the model a second time, in most cases, after a session moves into a worktree under .claude/worktrees with EnterWorktree or is resumed there
  • Fixed tool calls that never ran being counted as done in a claude.ai chat's summary line after you declined a permission prompt in a session that had restarted
  • Linux: Fixed the Bash edit diff showing an unchanged symlink as edited after Claude had read the file through it
  • Fixed resuming a session and /stats freezing for seconds when a transcript holds many damaged lines
  • Fixed a family name such as sonnet in --fallback-model being dropped when availableModels allows only an older version of it
  • Fixed keys lagging for seconds while /stats reads large session transcripts, also after the dialog is closed, and with debug logging on while a language server floods its stderr
  • Fixed a session failing when the cloud refused its default model and an availableModels list that isn't enforced named neither it nor an older model of that family
  • Fixed an enforced list of older models failing on Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Foundry when the first is refused: it now steps down to the next in that family, if listed newest first
  • Fixed opus failing on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Foundry behind a gateway that refuses a model in its own words: it now steps down to an older model that answers
  • Fixed the start-up model upgrade offer on Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform naming a model that your availableModels list leaves out
  • Fixed Bedrock sub-agents failing when your account lists no profile for their model in the parent's region: they now use the model's own profile, which can be outside that region
  • Fixed Foundry sessions leaving a model family when an admin's list blocks the version sonnet, opus or haiku points to: they now use its newest allowed version under a built-in or mapped name
  • Fixed the sonnet alias on Bedrock Mantle resolving to Haiku 4.5: it now means Sonnet 5, not Sonnet 5.5, and an account without Sonnet 5 gets an error, so enable it first
  • Fixed Ctrl+C at the prompt starting a new turn, and a double Ctrl+C not exiting, when a background agent it stopped had an unread subagent report
  • Fixed /install-github-app ticking a workflow again after going back with Esc
  • Fixed dictated text past 10,000 characters being lost
  • Fixed raw "JSON Parse error" and "The operation was aborted." API errors when the non-streaming retry got a broken response or was interrupted
  • Fixed Esc not stopping computer use between actions on macOS when Claude Code's window or an app you allowed is in front; an Esc meant for that app's popup now stops computer use instead
  • Fixed a rare hang when a helper command, such as an API key helper, ran past its time limit
  • Fixed selecting text in fullscreen pushing the footer's right-hand label onto a second row, which moved the text under the mouse and could copy the wrong line
  • Fixed a PreToolUse hook's reason for asking not showing on terminal Read, Grep, Glob, Edit and Write prompts (#102892, #105343)
  • Fixed temp_* folders piling up in ~/.claude/plugins/cache when a downloaded plugin couldn't be copied into place
  • Fixed --effort being ignored when starting an interactive session with --environment while CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is set to the same level
  • Fixed headless and cloud sessions reporting a foreground fork's Agent call as finished the moment the fork started
  • Fixed local MCP servers seeing a new session ID after a Remote Control session's process restarts
  • Fixed idle compaction being skipped for subscribers still well under their weekly limit
  • Fixed an @-mentioned text file with an extension being silently dropped when even its first 2,000 lines exceed the read limit; Claude is now told its size and how to read it
  • Fixed the plugin "not cached" error pointing to /plugin instead of /reload-plugins, the command that reloads plugins
  • Fixed self-hosted runner sessions failing their first clone under Anthropic-managed git when the machine's git config has an includeIf "gitdir:" or (git 2.44 to 2.46) "onbranch:" section
  • Fixed replies that start with phrases like "You've used" or "You've hit your" showing as a red usage limit error
  • Fixed a resumed conversation sometimes missing its last messages after a crash or kill on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Foundry and other third-party providers
  • Fixed NotebookEdit saving an invalid notebook when an edit changes a cell's type; turning a cell with attachments into code is now refused
  • Fixed a long README in a design system moved from standalone Claude Design losing its list of files to load when Claude starts a deck or design
  • Fixed MCP tool calls failing with "malformed task handle" when the server's task ID is longer than 128 characters; IDs of up to 1,024 characters now work
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed --configure-git sometimes reporting a hung git --version as a git that isn't on PATH
  • Fixed task ids being reused and deleted tasks coming back when several tasks were deleted or updated at once, and TaskGet listing completed tasks as blockers
  • Fixed stale and repeated rows in the fullscreen Ctrl+R history picker when prompts share a timestamp
  • Fixed Code Mode silently skipping a tool call whose input has a list of over 4,096 items, and freezing on a very large typed array in a tool's input, which is now refused
  • Fixed Code Mode leaving a message unanswered when it was typed during a command and Esc was pressed before Claude replied; the message now starts a new turn, which a second Esc stops
  • Fixed Code Mode not telling Claude when a slow command moved to the background and left its script with empty output, or of the time limit on background commands in claude -p and the Agent SDK
  • Fixed Code Mode sometimes waiting for minutes on a command that had already been stopped
  • Fixed a typed slash command's inline shell commands not running in Code Mode after a background script's output arrived
  • Fixed Code Mode sessions in the Agent SDK and claude -p sometimes losing Claude's last reply on resume after being stopped while a script was running
  • Remote Control: Fixed sessions hosted by the desktop app or VS Code showing as idle while /compact runs
  • Fixed a session sometimes losing its "needs input" status after a background task's report in Claude Desktop
  • Fixed Grep: -o missing an empty match at the end of a file with no last newline, -o with multiline adding an empty line or misnumbering lines in non-UTF-8 files, and -A and -B ignored beside a zero -C
  • Fixed unbinding a chord in keybindings.json still leaving its first key waiting for a second when it was spelled meta and bound as alt, or the reverse
  • Fixed moving an empty session to the background sometimes failing with "Couldn't load transcript from file"
  • Fixed OpenTelemetry reporting a failed mcp_server_connection event at each start for a built-in server that isn't turned on for the account
  • Fixed Esc not stopping a Bash command while it waited for its file diff in large or slow git repositories, which held the next message
  • Fixed pasted links and relative paths ending in an image file name appearing late and swallowing an Enter pressed right after
  • Fixed /mcp reconnect all and /mcp disable all counting a built-in server that isn't turned on for the account
  • Fixed interrupting a turn while a mod's turn.step hook was waiting showing "user-cancel" as an error instead of "Interrupted"
  • Fixed ~/.claude.json being reported as corrupted when another session was in the middle of saving it
  • Fixed web searches failing with an API error when Claude's list of allowed or blocked domains was empty or had duplicates
  • Fixed resuming a paused workflow in Code Mode waiting for minutes while other background work was running
  • Fixed subagents in Code Mode failing with "Agent stalled" and losing their command when a script ran for more than 10 minutes
  • Improved claude plugin marketplace add on Windows to wait and try again in some cases when another program, such as a virus scanner, briefly holds the downloaded files
  • Windows: Improved stability on some company PCs, where Claude Code could exit with no output shortly after start
  • Improved computer use setup: the Screen Recording permission prompt can now restart Claude Code and resume the chat
  • Improved computer use to take less context until Claude uses it
  • Improved the error when a proxy or gateway cuts or damages a compressed response: a turn now ends in plain words instead of raw "ZlibError fetching" text
  • Improved /context: shorter output in fullscreen, so the total is less likely to scroll off in a short window, and the legend names its unit once
  • Improved peak memory use and speed of /usage on machines with many recent sessions
  • Improved /permissions to refuse a rule that would be skipped at the next start, such as rm -rf with no tool name, and to show the reason
  • Improved resuming a session in Code Mode: Claude is now told up front that its earlier script variables are gone
  • Improved Claude in Code Mode to confirm before discarding worktree changes, to read artifact files before publishing them, and to update an existing artifact instead of creating a second one
  • Improved Code Mode's tool search to show long MCP tool descriptions whole where they fit, as a cut description could lead to wrong calls
  • Linux: Improved the Ctrl+V message to name the package to install (wl-clipboard or xclip) when images can't be read from the clipboard
  • Improved recovery for long conversations behind a proxy or gateway with a request size limit, where every message and /compact failed with a 413
  • Improved Glob speed in large local folders on Windows machines with 6 or more CPUs: folders are walked in parallel, and a search stopped at its time limit now lists what it found
  • Improved memory use when resuming a long conversation
  • Improved memory use at startup with MCP servers that list many tools
  • Improved memory use of claude -p and SDK-hosted sessions at the start of a conversation
  • Updated computer use on macOS to newer safety rules, so some actions are refused and typing can be slower
  • Changed terminal and VS Code sessions moved to Sonnet 5 or 5.5 on Bedrock Mantle, Agent Platform and Foundry to start in auto mode if no mode is set; set disableAutoMode to "disable" to stop it
  • Changed the sonnet model alias on Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry to Sonnet 5.5, and Foundry's opus alias to Opus 5.5; sonnet on Amazon Bedrock stays at Sonnet 4.5
  • Changed the default model on Microsoft Foundry to Sonnet 5.5: deploy claude-sonnet-5-5, or set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL to a model you have deployed
  • Changed sonnet and background requests on Google Cloud's Agent Platform to read VERTEX_REGION_CLAUDE_5_5_SONNET; with only the 4_5 variable set they go to CLOUD_ML_REGION or us-east5
  • Changed --model default and a Default pick to move to an older model when that model isn't available, instead of stopping with an error; in auto mode, only to a model auto mode accepts
  • Changed Microsoft Foundry: Claude Sonnet 4, Opus 4 and Opus 4.1 now count as retired, so step-downs stop above them and a pin to one warns that it was retired
  • Changed the Claude apps gateway's built-in model list: Sonnet 5.5 replaces Sonnet 4.5 as its second model, and Claude Desktop starts on it where a policy allows no Opus 4.6
  • Changed SDK and claude -p mid-turn messages to count as the user's where feature flags aren't fetched, as on clouds or with telemetry off, from Opus 4.8 on; mark relayed text isSynthetic: true
  • Changed computer-use to a reserved skill name on Macs with computer use on: your own skill or command of that name stops loading, and a start-up notice says to rename it
  • Changed the default OpenTelemetry service.name of desktop Code tab sessions to claude-code-desktop; update filters keyed on claude-code, or set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME to keep the old name
  • Changed OpenTelemetry tool_input to show only the length of text sent through SendUserMessage or Cowork's message tool, unless response logging is on (OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=1)
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: its prefix can now end in oat02- as well as oat01-. Update proxy rules and log scrubbers that match oat01-, and mask the whole value
  • Changed claude self-hosted-runner setup with no arguments on macOS and Linux to ask for the environment key in the terminal before Claude starts, and to hide it as you paste
  • Changed Claude Desktop's Code tab on Anthropic's API to ignore default, side-request, alias and subagent model ids not starting with claude in your own settings beside a gateway address
  • Changed Claude Desktop's Code tab on Anthropic's API to ignore a CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW under 200K in your own settings beside a gateway address; use /autocompact instead
  • Changed plan mode in the desktop app's Code tab and VS Code to ask for approval instead of refusing when no auto mode safety check can judge a command, for plans entered from Manual or Accept edits
  • Changed PgUp and Home to go to No on destructive questions, such as /clear from an agent's view
  • Changed /feedback drafts in the terminal to open on Not now, above separate rows to send the report alone or with the transcript
  • Changed tap-mode voice dictation to keep the microphone on until 60 seconds without new words or 10 minutes, up from 15 seconds and 2 minutes, then keep the text unsent; the next tap adds to it
  • Changed tap-mode voice dictation to stop when you send the prompt, and to stop and say why when you edit it, a panel covers it, or the connection or a separate recorder program is lost
  • Changed /schedule, permission prompts and /loop's cloud offer to say "cloud scheduled task" instead of "routine" or "cloud schedule"; /routines still works
  • Changed model switches from the Claude mobile app or claude.ai to keep the effort level you saved for the previous model when none is saved for the new one
  • Changed the hint a mod's PromptHint hook receives to leave out the hint for selected text when the fullscreen footer has a label on its right
  • Changed awsCredentialExport to time out after 10 minutes instead of waiting forever
  • [VSCode] Added a notification in more cases when closing a proposed diff leaves the edit unapplied, and stopped the diff notifications on a split copy of an answered diff
  • [VSCode] Added a warning when restoring a conversation with /rewind in the side bar stops a self-paced /loop
  • [VSCode] Added the installed version to the rows of Manage plugins
  • [VSCode] Fixed Rewind staying on "Checking code changes…" while Claude's process hung at its start
  • [VSCode] Fixed the model picker's arrow keys starting from the wrong row right after it opens, and screen readers not announcing its highlighted model when opened with /model or the command menu
  • [VSCode] Fixed the diff view's "Copy deleted line" and "Copy changed line" copying a different line than they name, and a double-click near the bottom copying unasked
  • [VSCode] Fixed the blocked microphone's tooltip being cut off, long addresses running out of Web Fetch rows, usage bars looking full in High Contrast, and a Thinking row jumping away when clicked
  • [VSCode] Fixed a second Logout in the same window reporting success while the first was still running, and added a Show logs button to the error when logout fails
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat showing no notice when a background command, agent, workflow or monitor finished while Claude was idle
  • [VSCode] Fixed forking a conversation, opening and saving memories, and creating project output styles failing on NTFS drives in VS Code 1.101 and 1.102 on Windows 11 24H2 and later
  • [VSCode] Fixed Web Fetch showing "Fetched from" with a success dot when the site returned an error or a redirect that wasn't followed
  • [VSCode] Fixed the compaction summary showing as your own prompt, and in Rewind and prompt history, after reloading, resuming or forking a compacted conversation
  • [VSCode] Fixed spinnerVerbs from Claude Code user and managed settings being ignored
  • [VSCode] Fixed right-to-left text from mods showing its punctuation on the wrong side, and a mod's band or pane filling only part of its width when the panel font has no box-drawing characters
  • [VSCode] Fixed an empty, locked editor pane staying beside the next file or Claude tab after the last Claude tab was closed
  • [VSCode] Fixed a session rename that cannot be saved reverting silently, and screen readers not hearing a session's status, which session is open or which groups are collapsed
  • [VSCode] Fixed a hidden panel's notice not naming the waiting session, Hebrew and Arabic questions reading out of order, and a question cut off when Claude's process ended showing only a red dot
  • [VSCode] Fixed a sign-in that failed with no error message returning to the sign-in screen with nothing shown, and an authentication error still looking current after you signed in again in that tab
  • [VSCode] Fixed the chat moving when a menu opened over some banners, and an agent's tool call count shrinking in long sessions; it now shows how many of the calls are listed
  • [VSCode] Fixed most links to files without an extension, to folders, and with a line and column doing nothing
  • [VSCode] Fixed queued messages and attached files showing in reverse order after a conversation was reopened
  • [VSCode] Fixed a question that ended in an error showing "Something went wrong" when its stored result had no text
  • [VSCode] Fixed redacted thinking showing as "Unsupported content type"
  • [VSCode] Fixed the message box not underlining the word that an input method (IME) is composing
  • [VSCode] Fixed a held Up key replacing an unsent message with an earlier prompt, and Down not bringing the message back after the recalled prompt got a new line or was cleared
  • [VSCode] Fixed /model completed with Tab sometimes switching the model, and closing the model picker right away when nothing is running
  • [VSCode] Improved the time it takes to open the Claude panel and long sessions, performance while long replies stream, and the speed of reading diagnostics in very large workspaces
  • [VSCode] Improved commands and one-line output opened in a plain text tab: they now wrap
  • [VSCode] Changed voice dictation to stop by itself after 60 seconds without recognized speech or 10 minutes, up from 15 seconds and 2 minutes, so the microphone can stay on longer
  • [VSCode] Changed voice dictation to stop, and say why, when the microphone stops sending audio or the panel stays hidden

title: v2.1.331
summary:
What's changed

  • Added Code Mode support in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
  • Added oidc.groups_jsonpath to the Claude apps gateway, to read groups from the matching entries of a list of objects with a small subset of JSONPath (RFC 9535)
  • Added an API connectivity section to claude doctor that reports whether the API can be reached, with the HTTP status or the error, or says why it wasn't tested
  • Added a notice when tap-mode voice dictation stops by itself, after 15 seconds without recognized speech or at its 2-minute limit
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_RESPONSE_COMPRESSION to ask for uncompressed model responses behind a proxy that cuts compressed ones off; not advised yet for self-hosted runners or Remote Control
  • Added CLAUDE_GATEWAY_IDP_CONNECT_BY_HOSTNAME=1 for Claude apps gateways: with oidc.use_proxy: true, sign-in requests hand the proxy an https IdP's hostname even with NO_PROXY set
  • Added gen_ai.usage.*, gen_ai.response.model and gen_ai.operation.name to claude_code.llm_request trace spans; gen_ai.usage.input_tokens includes prompt cache tokens
  • Added optionalDependencies to plugin manifests: plugins that install with the plugin listing them and can be disabled or uninstalled on their own
  • Fixed MCP tool calls hanging for up to 30 minutes on some malformed replies from a local or WebSocket server
  • Fixed PushNotification telling a headless run, such as a scheduled one, that the terminal was active in its first minute, instead of saying whether a mobile push was requested
  • Fixed /install-github-app skipping the repository step after setup warnings when no repository was found, and Esc not going back from its workflow list and sign-in steps
  • Fixed one-line tool results cut with no ellipsis in narrow windows, Markdown stars in the Auto mode tab of /permissions, and a hook's reason to stop a forked skill showing twice
  • Fixed /diff hiding its key hints and not selecting files in windows of 24 to 26 rows, and leaving out files added with git add -N in a repository with no commits
  • Fixed the first-run theme list showing too few themes in short windows, and /usage and other tall screens coming out garbled there
  • Fixed /bug in fullscreen hiding its Yes and No answers behind a long report, and Yes staying out of view in very short windows
  • Fixed /compact and auto-compact sometimes losing part of the conversation summary when the summary quoted certain XML tags
  • Fixed Claude not being told when permission rules on the Agent tool dropped its queued message to a subagent that had already ended
  • Fixed a Remote Control message sometimes showing above the reply that was finishing when it was sent
  • Fixed Stop hooks that read the transcript missing the last reply in Claude Desktop; SubagentStop hooks now wait for it too
  • Fixed turns and subagents failing in cloud sessions, or timing out on long replies elsewhere, when a reply went silent while Claude was still thinking; Claude Code now tries the request once more
  • Fixed Esc and Stop waiting about a minute or more when the contents of a cloud or network file that Claude is reading stall
  • Fixed Code Mode sessions resumed with --resume or --continue in another permission mode losing thinking and the prompt cache; one begun in a mode that asks keeps that mode's limits on scripts
  • Fixed Code Mode sending a request about every second when a ! or slash command was typed while a script was running
  • Fixed an interrupted or failed plugin update leaving a partial plugin folder that later loaded with skills or other components missing (#102186)
  • Windows: Fixed file writes on FAT32 and exFAT drives asking for permission every time in some plugin sessions
  • Fixed Claude failing to read a notebook that has a null output or an error output with no traceback
  • Fixed a rewind deleting files after a restore had failed
  • Fixed auto mode sometimes refusing Claude's call to stop a /loop, which left the next wake-up to fire
  • Fixed a Workflow agent's background shells and MCP servers sometimes being left running after it handed back its report
  • Windows: Fixed /desktop downloading the older Claude Desktop installer, and asking for an update when an older install's folder was left behind
  • Fixed claude plugin install, marketplace add and similar commands hanging with no output when managed settings needed an approval that could not be asked for
  • Fixed a permission rule on a subagent's model, such as Agent(model:*), blocking Claude's follow-up message to a subagent started on this version with no model named
  • Fixed PermissionRequest hooks not saving Skill(name:*) allow rules outside local settings
  • Fixed "Ask your admin" asking to raise your own limit when your team's pooled group budget blocked you, and saying "Request sent" when an admin had approved your request in the last few minutes
  • Fixed Code Mode losing the middle of a long script output; Claude now gets a path to the uncut text (#111373)
  • Fixed hold-to-talk dictation stopping early and losing words when Claude Code was busy
  • Fixed Code Mode with --bare not telling Claude what its scripts can call
  • Fixed a crash when a custom API endpoint returned a tool call with no tool name; the call now fails with an error and the session continues
  • Windows: Fixed a possible crash when the machine is almost out of memory
  • Fixed the CLI freezing on some replies, and quoted text sometimes going missing or showing twice
  • Windows: Fixed Claude Code refusing to start when managed settings in the registry contain non-ASCII characters such as Japanese (#93280)
  • Windows: Fixed Remote Control clients showing no steps for a new subagent
  • Fixed @-mentions written as @file#10-12 attaching the whole file instead of those lines
  • Fixed Claude misreading a pasted artifact invitation link; it now asks you to accept the invitation and paste the artifact's own link
  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands sometimes failing to start on a full temp disk, for sandboxes whose file rules keep commands out of the temp directory
  • Improved typing speed in screen reader mode, most of all in long sessions
  • Improved start-up time: a session started soon after another no longer waits for the model list, and one outside a git repository without .claude/settings.local.json no longer waits on git
  • Windows: Improved the speed of the first Bash command in a session on machines with no custom shell start-up files
  • Improved the plugin auto-update notice to name plugins it newly installs as dependencies, separately from updated plugins
  • Improved Code Mode tool search to show more of an MCP tool's description, with its limits, formats and defaults
  • Improved the Console sign-in link shown by /login and claude auth login --console: it is now much shorter
  • Improved Claude's list of your artifacts: it now marks web pages, so Claude is less likely to try opening one with the Claude Docs connector
  • Improved the folder trust prompts in short terminals: fullscreen /cd and /add-dir show their choices in fewer rows, and the prompt at launch keeps the folder path in view when it has many warnings
  • Changed the questions for stopping auto-connect in /ide and for /clear, /compact or /rewind in a subagent's view to list Yes first; they still start on No, so Down then Enter now answers No
  • Changed what a PermissionDenied hook's retry: true tells Claude: make the refused call again only if you asked for that call
